entries.answer: Tayo means we, and it refers to a group that includes the speaker. It is also the polite form of the verb stand, so the word genuinely does two different jobs. The plural kami is the group excluding the speaker, and ako is the speaker alone, so Filipino marks exactly who is included rather than leaving it to context.

patterns: kami or tayo which is correct
entries.answer: Kami means we or they, and it refers to a group that excludes the speaker. The distinction from tayo is the single most consistent feature of Filipino pronouns, as kami excludes the listener and the speaker while tayo includes both. In practice tayo is the normal everyday choice.

entries.answer: Natin means we or us, specifically us including the speaker, and it is the object and possessive form of tayo. Namin is the exclusive equivalent. The natin and nila forms are the ones learners find hardest, because English collapses them all into a single we and us while Filipino keeps them apart.

patterns: kayo or ikaw which to use
entries.answer: Kayo means you, and it addresses the person or people being spoken to. With po it becomes the polite form, and kayo po is the respectful address used to a customer, an elder or anyone being treated with respect. It is the word to use with strangers, whereas ikaw is what you use with friends, family and children.

patterns: ikaw or kayo which is polite
entries.answer: Ikaw means you, singular and familiar. It is the form used with friends, family, children and anyone you are comfortable with, while kayo is the polite and plural form. Using ikaw to a stranger can come across as rude or too familiar, which is why kayo is the safer default in a shop or an office.
